x-bump-note: 3.1.0 -> 3.2.0 (top-level-array-additive) adds the optional top-level array `reviewed_targets`, admitting the closed prefix set uncommitted:/untracked:/working-tree:/diff-artifact: for non-committed review targets a resolved commit range cannot express. `reviewed_range` is byte-unchanged — not its pattern, not its description — by deliberate ruling: the alternative (a discriminated union inside `reviewed_range`) would have been enum-value-additive, holding unconditionally on the x-schema-version axis and forcing claude-klabauter to re-vendor before any reviewer could emit the new form; a separate top-level array keeps the rejection of `..HEAD` and other re-resolving refs living in a pattern this bump does not touch. The bump is structurally additive and non-breaking on shape, but remains HOLDING for claude-klabauter specifically: the non-holding carve-out requires an affirmative, on-record consumer declaration of structural tolerance for unknown top-level arrays, and claude-klabauter has declared none against this schema — claude-klabauter must re-vendor before its reviewers emit `reviewed_targets`. Mirror of run-report.schema.json's own 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 bump, kept in step with it. Spec: docs/plans/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-non-committed-review-targets.md; DR-156. Prior: 3.0.0 -> 3.1.0 (enum-value-additive) widens `reviewed_range.items`'s pattern to admit an optional trailing `~<N>` (N a positive integer) on the LEFT endpoint, alongside the existing `^`. `<sha>~1` and `<sha>^` name the same commit for a single-parent commit, so the two forms are equally deterministic and the pattern's own hex-anchored `^...$` rationale is unaffected — this is a widen of which left-endpoint suffix is admitted, not a change to what the anchoring rejects. Classified enum-value-additive (the closest vocabulary member; the pattern functions as a closed value-shape enumeration rather than a JSON Schema `enum` keyword, and this bump has the identical property that closed-vocabulary class describes: previously-rejected strings now validate, every previously-valid string stays valid, no field added or removed, no other value's semantics changed) rather than inventing a fifth vocabulary term. Ask 1 of cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-14-claude-klabauter-em-reviewed-range-pattern-and-direction-blind-parity-gate.md: claude-klabauter's pre-vendor corpus sweep against the incoming 3.0.0 pattern found 53 files/22 values, 10 rejects, 6 of which were fully-resolved `<sha>~1..<sha>` hex ranges the pattern omitted by oversight, not by design (state/audits/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-pattern-corpus-sweep.md). The mirror of run-report.schema.json's own 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0 bump, kept in step with it. Prior: 2.1.0 -> 3.0.0 (major) narrowed `reviewed_range.items` with the hex-SHA-anchored range pattern in the first place, rejecting symbolic refs (HEAD, HEAD~3, branch and tag names). Safe to land now and only now: zero on-disk sidecars carry `reviewed_range` in frontmatter (verified by grep at bump time), so no existing record can be invalidated. Ask 1 of cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-13-claude-klabauter-em-reviewed-range-attacked-two-asks-back.md; adopted per docs/decisions/DR-156-reviewer-attests-at-review-time-is-admissible-evidence.md.
description: Pre-scaffolded code-reviewer self-persist findings sidecar. FRONTMATTER-BEARING as of v2.0.0 (docs/plans/2026-07-24-reviewer-sidecar-provisioning-reconciliation.md): coordinator-doc-new --type review-findings's self-scaffold fallback now emits the same frontmatter superset block as coordinator_core.subagent_sandbox.provision_report.py's provisioned (common) path -- status/agent_type/spawned_at/lead_session_id/divergence/commits/dispatch_feed -- so both producers are shape-identical and this schema needs no match_mode:no-frontmatter special-case (that mode existed solely to suppress the missing-frontmatter warning for the old bare-prose shape, which does not exist). required:[status] mirrors run-report.schema.json's own required set (the superset schema that also applies_to state/subagent-share/*/*.md) -- a review-findings file now satisfies BOTH schemas' required fields identically; this schema's applies_to glob stays the MORE SPECIFIC of the two (discriminated by the 'codereview-slice' filename token that only coordinator-doc-new's self-scaffold produces) so routing_strategy: most-specific-glob-wins (see artifact-shape-contract.schema.json) still resolves a review-findings file to THIS schema over the broader run-report one, without either schema rejecting it. Each self-scaffolded file is scoped to one code-reviewer dispatch (one review slice). The reviewer scaffolds its own sidecar here, replaces the FINDINGS sentinel with its full findings body via a single Edit, then returns a path pointer to the EM. The EM never absorbs the findings body into its own context. Lives at state/subagent-share/<session-id>/ -- the DR-091 one-home shared with every other typed subagent sidecar (run-report, staff-eng-review, assessment), not a review-findings-specific directory. Path formula (self-scaffold only): state/subagent-share/<session-id>/YYYY-MM-DD-codereview-slice<ID>-<SLUG>.md where <session-id> = the harness session id (coordinator-doc-new's _resolve_session_id(), sanitized), <ID> = --slice arg (alphanumeric + dashes, e.g. 'Z', 'A', '2a') and <SLUG> = sanitized --scope arg (comma-separated paths lowercased + non-alnum -> dash). Example: --slice Z --scope tests/x.py -> state/subagent-share/<session-id>/2026-06-30-codereview-sliceZ-tests-x-py.md. Sole self-scaffold producer: coordinator-doc-new --type review-findings --slice <id> --scope <comma-paths>. Registering this schema fires SCHEMAED-DOC-GENERATE-OBLIGATION for the self-scaffold path; the provisioned (common) path is produced by the engine, not this CLI. Do NOT write to state/subagent-share/ by hand. The FINDINGS sentinel (<!-- FINDINGS -->) is the anchor the reviewer replaces via a single Edit; note this sentinel text is distinct from provision_report.py's own review-findings template sentinel (a pre-existing, out-of-scope-here producer divergence). A surviving sentinel after review indicates a no-op or an aborted write. Distinct from state/review-trail/*.json (JSON trail records, produced by coordinator-write-review-trail.sh) -- this schema governs the markdown findings body only. Spec backlink: cross-repo/inbox/2026-07-01-reviewer-selfpersist-confinement-redirect.md. Spec backlink (subagent-share migration + frontmatter unification): docs/plans/2026-07-24-reviewer-sidecar-provisioning-reconciliation.md

status.description: Subagent lifecycle state. Mirrors run-report.schema.json's status property (same enum, same 'open' initial value written by both producers).

items.description: Hex-SHA-anchored range only — full or abbreviated hex SHAs on both endpoints (4-64 hex chars, covering both sha1's 40-char and sha256-format repos' 64-char object ids via `--object-format=sha256`), joined by `..` or `...`, with an optional trailing `^` or `~<N>` (N a positive integer, no bare `~`) on the LEFT endpoint only (the `<sha>^..<sha>` form the per-slice partition forces; `<sha>~<N>` names the same commit as `<sha>^` for a single-parent commit and is admitted as an equivalent, deterministic left-endpoint form). Anchored with `^...$` deliberately: JSON Schema `pattern` is UNANCHORED by default, and an unanchored pattern here would admit a symbolic ref merely containing a hex-shaped substring. Any non-hex-shaped symbolic ref — `HEAD`, `HEAD~3`, most branch names, most tags — is REJECTED: it re-resolves differently on every read (coordinator_core's own `review_trail_write.py` `_resolve_ref_to_sha` pays to prevent exactly this — a record left carrying a literal `HEAD` 'silently grows to swallow every commit landed after it was written, with no reviewer having opened any of them'). A hex-shaped branch or tag name (e.g. `cafe1234..beef5678`) is indistinguishable from a resolved SHA range at this syntax layer and is NOT caught here; that residual is the consuming seam's job via a `git rev-list` set-subset check against the frozen review range, not this pattern's.

reviewed_range.description: Commit ranges (git rev-list syntax, e.g. 'abc123^..abc123') this reviewer attests to having ACTUALLY READ during this dispatch. Mirrors run-report.schema.json's own `reviewed_range` property. WRITE-OWNER: the exact inverse of run-report.schema.json's `commits` property — written by the reviewing subagent ONLY, never by the EM, and never by a closing session, under any circumstance; an EM-written value is the retired PM vouch under a new name (docs/decisions/DR-156-reviewer-attests-at-review-time-is-admissible-evidence.md). ABSENCE: omitted entirely when nothing was reviewed — no empty-array sentinel, no 'reviewed nothing' value; a present-but-empty array asserts something nobody claimed. ADMITS, NEVER REPLACES: this field admits a state/review-trail/*.json record whose `sha_range` (coordinator/schemas/review-trail.schema.json) falls inside an attested range here — it does not credit coverage, does not duplicate or re-implement the trail record, and changes nothing about what counts as reviewed. An attested range here that EXCEEDS the dispatching slice's own frozen-diff range (the `--range` persisted by `freeze-review-diff.py`'s `_open_pending_trail_record` at freeze time) is a DEFECT in the attestation, not a valid superset claim — admission is decided as a `git rev-list` SET-SUBSET test over enumerated commits (`set(rev-list(sha_range)) ⊆ set(rev-list(attested_i))`, with each `attested_i` itself within the slice's frozen range), never a string comparison of range endpoints — string-comparing `abc^..abc` to `abc^..def` would silently mis-admit across a merge. PRE-FIELD REVIEWERS: a reviewer that predates this field carries no `reviewed_range` key at all; a consumer date-discriminates that case via the sidecar's own `spawned_at` timestamp rather than inventing a `reviewed_range_version` field. LIST, NOT SINGLE: an array because the foreign-session partition already forces per-slice <sha>^..<sha> records; a single-range field would make widening the cheapest way to comply. Spec backlink: DR-156 (above); docs/plans/2026-08-13-reviewed-range-reviewer-attestation-field.md.

items.description: Closed prefix set only — one of `uncommitted:`, `untracked:`, `working-tree:`, or `diff-artifact:`, followed by a non-empty, whitespace-free, comma-free path (repo-relative BY CONVENTION, not enforced — see NEGATIVE-SPEC below). Anchored with `^...$` deliberately, for the same reason `reviewed_range`'s item pattern is: JSON Schema `pattern` is UNANCHORED by default, and an unanchored pattern here would admit any string merely CONTAINING a valid prefix — including a hybrid like `1175181e5e6f..working-tree`, which is exactly the hazard this field must not readmit. `uncommitted:<path>` names a tracked file carrying uncommitted changes; `untracked:<path>` names a file not in the index; `working-tree:<path>` names the working-tree state of a path (prefix-form only); `diff-artifact:<path>` names a standalone .diff/.patch file that was read. NEGATIVE-SPEC: the pattern does not enforce repo-relativity of the path segment (it admits `../` and leading `/`); a consumer must never join a `reviewed_targets` value to a filesystem path — it is attestation text, not a path input.

reviewed_targets.description: Non-committed review targets this reviewer attests to having ACTUALLY READ during this dispatch. Mirrors run-report.schema.json's own `reviewed_targets` property — the sibling of `reviewed_range` for work with no resolvable commit range. WRITE-OWNER: written by the reviewing subagent ONLY, never the EM, never a closing session — the same inverse-of-`commits` rule `reviewed_range` carries. ABSENCE: omitted entirely when there was no non-committed target reviewed — no empty-array sentinel, no 'reviewed nothing' value. ADMITS, NEVER REPLACES: this field admits a record the same way `reviewed_range` does — it credits nothing and duplicates nothing in state/review-trail/*.json. LIST, NOT SINGLE: one target per array element; a comma-separated list packed into a single element (e.g. `working-tree: a.py, b.py`) is malformed and the item pattern rejects it. NEVER A COMMIT RANGE: a resolved commit range belongs in `reviewed_range` and only there — this field NEVER holds one, and a hybrid `<sha>..working-tree` value is REJECTED by both fields' patterns because its right endpoint re-resolves on every read, which is the same `..HEAD` hazard `reviewed_range`'s anchoring exists to reject, wearing different clothes. Spec backlink: DR-156; docs/plans/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-non-committed-review-targets.md.
